title: k-NN, k-means and the decision stump

wrong.zscore_uses_test_statistics.py: zscore standardises with the test set's mean and std, leaking test data into preprocessing and breaking train/test consistency
wrong.knn_picks_farthest.py: knn_predict votes among the k farthest points instead of the k nearest
wrong.knn_tie_picks_largest_label.py: knn_predict breaks vote ties toward the larger label instead of the smaller
wrong.kmeans_empty_cluster_becomes_nan.py: kmeans takes the mean of an empty cluster, producing NaN centers
wrong.kmeans_single_round.py: kmeans stops after one round whatever `iters` says
wrong.gini_forgets_square.py: gini computes 1 - sum(p) which is always 0 instead of 1 - sum(p^2)
wrong.split_unweighted_children.py: best_split averages the two child impurities instead of weighting by child size
wrong.split_threshold_at_value.py: best_split returns a data value as the threshold instead of the midpoint between neighbours

hints: Distances: (X_test[:, None, :] - X_train[None, :, :]) has shape (m, n, d); square and sum over the last axis for squared distances, which rank neighbours the same as Euclidean. np.argsort(..., kind='stable') gives the tie rule for free; np.bincount(labels).argmax() gives the smaller-label rule.

k-means is two steps in a loop: assign each point to the nearest center (argmin over axis 1), then recompute each center as the mean of its members. Guard the empty-cluster case so you never average zero points.

A stump scans thresholds between consecutive distinct sorted values. For each, impurity after the split is (n_left * gini(left) + n_right * gini(right)) / n; the gain is the parent's impurity minus that. Keep the first threshold that beats the best gain so far.
